svg.title: webrarian
svg.desc: A hex sticker cut straight out of a cast-iron library book stack, in deep brick-red, bone iron and near-black oxblood, with the lights dimmed for night. There is no building and no roof: the shelf decks run off every edge of the hexagon, so the ranges plainly continue past the sticker. This is a shelf someone uses. The books do not stand to a rule — the top of each row is a skyline; two slim spines have slumped against the fat folios beside them; short piles of books lie flat across the heads of the uprights, filling the space under the deck; one folio stands proud of the shelf edge and casts a shadow, another is pushed back into the shade; the spines have crowned backs, head and tail caps, raised bands and gilt fillets, and one folio carries a pale call-number label at its foot. Underneath the life, the four full rows are still four bytes: a fat bone folio is a 1 bit and a slim dark spine is a 0 bit, and read top to bottom they spell 00 61 73 6D, the magic bytes that open every WebAssembly binary. Nothing announces this; you have to count. The wordmark webrarian is cast into a bone range-end plate bolted into the bottom shelf.
